title: Cardinal Billing Account Late Fee Schedule by Pay Plan
content:
The Cardinal Billing Account late fee figures differ by pay plan. Billing rules refer to the first column as "the pay plan's late fee".

| Pay plan | Late fee | Grace days after the due date (calendar days) | Most late fees charged in one policy term | Courtesy late fee waivers in a rolling 12 months |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Direct Bill Monthly Plan | $15.00 | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| Cardinal Card Autopay Monthly Plan | $10.00 | 5 | 3 | 1 |
| Cardinal EFT Autopay Monthly Plan | $10.00 | 5 | 3 | 1 |
| Cardinal Three-Pay Plan | $15.00 | 5 | 2 | 1 |
| Cardinal Two-Pay Plan | $15.00 | 7 | 1 | 1 |
| Cardinal Paid-in-Full Plan | $10.00 | 7 | 1 | 1 |

## Notes

- Grace days are counted in calendar days after the due date of the installment.
- The per-term figure is the largest number of late fees charged in one policy term on the plan.
- The courtesy figure is the number of late fees that may be waived on request in a rolling 12 months; on the Cardinal Direct Bill Monthly Plan it is 0, so no courtesy waiver is available on that plan.

## Quick comparisons

- Longest grace: 7 calendar days, on the Cardinal Two-Pay Plan and the Cardinal Paid-in-Full Plan.
- Shortest grace: 3 calendar days, on the Cardinal Direct Bill Monthly Plan.
- A plan with a cap of 1 (Cardinal Two-Pay Plan, Cardinal Paid-in-Full Plan) charges at most one late fee in a term; the Cardinal Three-Pay Plan at most 2; the three monthly plans at most 3.
